description: Research pebble; write findings into the repo docs. Related existing pebbles: egocentric datasets research voice-50a87f8c and robotics datasets research voice-c7c6c5dc (build on them, don't duplicate). Jake's plan: an open-source data collection system. A handheld gripper (easy to use by hand, logging motor and finger positions) plus camera glasses for egocentric video. He and others use the grippers and glasses, or just the glasses, to collect egocentric manipulation data. The hardware is sold cheaply or given away, and the data is sold. Research: (a) which camera glasses work for this: open access to raw video, frame rate and resolution, field of view, IMU, stereo or depth, eye tracking, battery, price, and whether data can be pulled off without vendor lock-in, e.g. Meta Project Aria Gen 2, Ray-Ban Meta, Snap Spectacles, Brilliant Labs, Xreal, or head-mounted GoPro/fisheye cameras as in UMI; (b) what companies buying robotics or egocentric data look for and pay: format (LeRobot, RLDS, MCAP), fidelity (fps, resolution, calibration, time sync, action/proprio labels, depth, hand pose, language annotations), task diversity, licensing and consent and PII, volume, and who is buying (labs, data brokers such as Scale, Encord, and the newer egocentric data marketplaces) at what prices; (c) prior art to learn from: UMI (Universal Manipulation Interface), DexUMI, Project Aria / Ego-Exo4D, and any open data-collection hardware projects. End with a concrete recommendation for glasses, data format, and a minimum spec.

results.identified_issue: Glasses verdict hinges on hand_1_0.md §3 (same stereo pair on human and robot) — that rules out every consumer glasses (all mono) and Aria (not purchasable, research terms). Ego-OSCAR specs read from the arXiv PDF (2608.08285): Dexcin global-shutter stereo 1280x720@30, 126°, 42 mm, ICM-20948 @120 Hz, 0.7 ms residual, ~USD 200 BOM, Apache-2.0 software; hardware license wording is 'permissively licensed', not checked file-by-file. Prices/pay rates are vendor/press figures, unverified. Aria Gen 2 RGB spec is single-source; Ray-Ban Meta price and GoPro battery unverified; DexUMI license not checked. Gripper 6-DoF pose without a gripper camera (tag cube tracked by head stereo) is an untested proposal. Not legal advice on BIPA/GDPR.
results.summary: Wrote plans/egocentric_data_collection.md: no glasses you can buy fit, so build an Ego-OSCAR-style stereo head rig (~$200, open), record MCAP and sell LeRobot v3, with a 10-line minimum spec
results.detailed_description:
Research is in plans/egocentric_data_collection.md and linked from the README. It builds on egocentric_datasets.md, robot_datasets.md, handheld_gripper.md and shared_stereo_glasses.md instead of repeating them.

Glasses: none you can buy fit. Ray-Ban Meta's developer stream is mono 720p30 over Bluetooth. Mentra Live is the most open consumer pair, but it's mono. Halo stores no video. Snap Specs are stereo, but they're $2,195 and capture runs inside Snap's sandbox. Aria Gen 2 has the best sensors but isn't for sale, and Meta's Aria data is non-commercial. A head-mounted GoPro is what UMI uses, but it's mono and rolling-shutter, so it breaks your rule that the robot carries the same stereo pair the person wears.

The fit is Ego-OSCAR, an open head rig published in Aug 2026 with about $200 of off-the-shelf parts. It has a hardware-synced global-shutter stereo pair (720p per eye at 30 fps, 126° field of view), an IMU synced to the cameras within a measured 0.7 ms, and a small Linux board that records to an SD card. It was field-proven over 550 hours with 25 contributors.

My recommendation: copy that rig and read the STS3215 gripper on the same board and clock. Put the identical stereo module on the robot's head. The glasses-only version is the same rig without the gripper, not a second consumer product.

Buyers: frontier labs, robot-model companies and world-model companies, plus brokers like Scale (Harness), Lightwheel, Build AI, truelabel and micro1. Raw egocentric video sells for roughly $15–22 per hour and annotated video for $30–40, with listings up to ~$135. Teleop robot data costs over $100 per hour. Contributor pay in India fell about 30% this year, so plain video is a commodity. Our edge is synced stereo plus real gripper actions plus a clean consent chain. These prices come from vendor and press sources and are unverified.

Format: record MCAP as the master copy and ship LeRobot v3 exports, with a published schema doc.

The doc ends with a 10-line minimum spec and six next steps:
- build one rig
- add the gripper read
- pilot an AprilTag cube for the gripper's pose
- write the exporter
- record about 5 hours and get two buyer quotes
- get a lawyer's read on consent and BIPA/GDPR

Open question: how to get the gripper's 6-DoF pose without putting a camera on it. My proposal is a tag cube tracked by the head cameras, and it's untested.

summary: Research which camera glasses suit Jake's open-source egocentric data collection system, paired with a handheld gripper, and what buyers want and pay. Write findings into the repo docs, building on the existing dataset pebbles, ending with a recommendation for glasses, format, and minimum spec.
